content: Side Effects: Stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea may occur while taking this medication. These effects are usually mild and temporary. However, if they persist or worsen, contact your doctor promptly. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea. This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but can occur. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. Precautions: Before taking cefadroxil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporins. Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefadroxil may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. If you are using the suspension form of this medication, be aware that it may contain sugar. Use caution if you have diabetes or any condition requiring you to limit sugar intake. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Cefadroxil passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefadroxil may cause false positive results in certain diabetic urine testing products (such as cupric sulfate-type tests). It may also affect the results of certain laboratory tests. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctors that you are using this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Usage and Monitoring: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney function tests) may be performed while you are taking this medication to monitor your progress or check for side effects. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store the capsules or tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. If you are using the suspension form, store it in the refrigerator and discard any unused portion after 14 days. Do not freeze the suspension. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for more details on how to safely discard your product. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
